nodes.title: Does a source rule confer a susceptibility to the complex phenotype on its refinements?
nodes.summary: Well posed only inside an explicit finite family. In the height-one strip fibers the base ECA predicts its preimages' phenotype distribution, and across all 64 fibers that dependence is non-additive in the six exposed bits on the spreading axis (birth-survival interactions) while additive on the persistence axis; the affine property of the base is irrelevant. 110 has no fiber in this family.

nodes.title: A base rule's height-one fiber is enriched or depleted in the persistence × spreading phenotype
nodes.summary: 512-rule samples of the fibers over ECAs 54, 22, 0, 90, 204 measured at height two have both-positive fractions 0.47, 0.37, 0.25, 0.22, 0.07 (Kruskal–Wallis on S* p ≈ 1e-40, descriptive). HighLife and Life sit inside their fibers' 10th–90th percentile bands. One contract, one density, one strip height. Across all 64 fibers (128 rules each) the both-positive fraction spans 0.05 to 0.51 and is non-additive in the exposed bits on the spreading axis; the 0/90 ordering did not replicate on fresh samples. A handed family whose height-one restriction is onto all 256 ECAs gives rule 110 a fiber (2^24 rules): it is both-positive at 0.543, tied at the top with its mirror 124 and with 54, far above 30 at 0.273, and the enrichment is on the persistence axis rather than spreading. A base's own 1D phenotype predicts its fiber's on both axes across all 256 bases. Chirality is not detectable: the mirror fiber is indistinguishable. A matched base-by-completion grid decomposes the persistence axis: history gain is set by the base (variance component 0.040 against the completion's 0.012) and retention by the completion (0.022 against 0.035); history gain anticorrelates between distant bases and is not bit-additive at all, and at height four a persistence-only control overtakes 110, so the conferral tracks the base's 1D history gain rather than its class. The mechanism is now known: an exactly invariant equal-row set on which the strip is the base rule makes history gain a mixture, so beam proximity mediates transfer between bases and the sign of each base's response explains the anticorrelation. The refinement's contribution is finally in a readable basis: twelve pairwise exclusive-ors of its free table entries decide one-step healing on the beam and, through an edge lemma, growth and survival at every step. That also explains why no linear model on the raw bits ever worked.

nodes.title: The equal-row set of a height-two strip is exactly invariant, and the strip is the base rule on it
nodes.summary: On a height-two cylinder the vertical wrap sends both off-rows onto the other row, so a state with equal rows has Moore count 3L+2C+3R and west neighbour L, making its condition index 16C+8L+(2L+2C+3R) — exactly the height-one exposed index. Those entries are fixed by the base ECA and unreachable by any completion, so equal rows stay equal and the strip acts as the base rule there. A closed, shift-invariant, F-invariant subsystem conjugate to the base elementary automaton. Verified exactly for sixteen bases over 256 steps at heights two and three. It makes history gain a mixture of the base's own one-dimensional value on the beam and a completion-set value off it, which mediates transfer between bases and explains the observed anticorrelation.

nodes.title: One-step healing on the beam is three pairwise bit-equalities; twelve in all, rank eleven
nodes.summary: Flipping one cell of a height-two beam state changes exactly six reads, and no post-flip read lands on an exposed entry, so the damage is carried entirely by free table entries. Healing in one step is A(LL,L) and B(L,R) and C(R,RR), each a required equality between two free entries: twelve equalities of GF(2) rank eleven, giving 2,048 signature classes of 8,192 refinements and a thirteen-dimensional universal-healer subspace, with expected one-step healing exactly 1/8. The A pairs are one table index apart, B fourteen, C six. An edge lemma extends the factorization to every step through the edges of any defect cluster, so A governs leftward growth, C rightward growth and B isolated survival; hence A or C never holding implies transverse extinction zero, both always holding implies confinement, and all twelve holding implies immediate healing. Verified by enumeration and as a gating control.

nodes.title: Which table entries a dense strip column reads is decided by the two rows' popcount difference
nodes.summary: At height two both rows of a column read one table entry each. With Delta the difference of the rows' three-cell popcounts, Delta = 0 makes both reads exposed entries owned by the base ECA, |Delta| = 1 makes both lit, and |Delta| >= 2 makes both dark. Enumerating the 64 six-bit windows gives 8 trivially agreeing cases and 28 unordered pairs: 6 exposed, 15 lit, 7 dark, with no mixed pair. This characterizes the single-defect algebra's 8/14/10 entry partition rather than enumerating it. GF(2) ranks 11 and 7 over 24 free entries leave exactly 64 completions satisfying every free constraint, one per connected component; disagreement then survives only through blind columns. Beta-all-hold is exactly the 16 totalistic rules, which collapse any state in one step; under rule 204 and rule 51 the residual is exactly the width-two anti-phase runs of the initial disagreement field, giving agree = 1 - 2*N_ap/W and a bit-identical median between those two bases.

nodes.title: An isolated defect under confinement is a sixteen-state automaton with a two-bit input
nodes.summary: When a refinement satisfies the two edge constraints, an isolated defect's west flank reads the A pair, the defect column the B pair, and the east flank the C pair, while the columns two out read exposed entries with agreeing windows. The state (west, the two row values, east) therefore evolves deterministically under a two-bit input supplied by the background. The greatest input-closed set of defect states (SAFE) and the least set closed under every input leading into it (DOOMED) partition the 57,344 confined refinements into 24,576 with a SAFE state, 28,672 with neither, and 4,096 entirely DOOMED. Verified against the real step with zero mismatches of 22,270. On the four bases whose background is frozen the input sequence is fixed by the base alone, and iterating the automaton predicts every one of 6,144 transverse trials' healing step exactly; across all 36 bases the partition bounds the extinction fraction with zero violations of 1,728.

nodes.title: Two defect clusters are independent only for as many steps as they are columns apart
nodes.summary: Under the confinement constraints the defect set never grows, but a cluster perturbs the agreeing background around it, because its flanks take the values the constraint pairs force rather than the values the base rule would produce. That perturbation travels at speed one, so two clusters separated by s agreeing columns evolve independently for t < s and not beyond: the first mismatch between the joint field and the union of isolated ones never precedes step s (minimum 4, 6, 8 at s = 4, 6, 8), and does not appear within 128 steps once s is at least 12. No fixed separation gives all-time independence. Established by refuting two successive stronger claims, the second made by the executing session at freeze; the refuting check used a persistent cell rather than a uniform draw, which is why earlier verification missed it.
